newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians, Israeli soldiers clash in Bethlehem.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians, Israeli soldiers clash in Bethlehem.

text.p: Palestinians protesting against Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem clashed with Israeli soldiers in the West Bank town of Bethlehem on Monday, witnesses said.
They said Israeli soldiers fired tear gas at more than 100 stone-throwing Palestinians who attacked troops guarding the tomb of the biblical matriarch Rachel at the northern entrance of Bethlehem.
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
An Israeli army spokesman said he was checking the report.
Israel's work on building 6,500 housing units for Jews on the outskirts of East Jerusalem last week has angered Palestinians, sparking almost daily demonstrations in several areas in the West Bank.
Scores of Palestinians have been wounded by rubber bullets or overcome by tear gas during the confrontations, mainly in the town of Hebron and in Bethlehem.
The violence came against the backdrop of heightened tensions over a Tel Aviv suicide bombing on Friday in which a Moslem militant killed three Israeli women.
In the Gaza Strip, about 1,000 Palestinians marched in a peaceful demonstration to protest against Israel's continued detention of about 3,000 Palestinian prisoners, witnesses said.
